test_title: SSC MTS Official Paper (Held On: 14 Jun, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

(They have been) dejected when he arrived, but now they sparkle with enthusiasm.
solution:
The correct answer is "**They had been**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence uses the present perfect tense, "They have been dejected."
 
• **However, the past perfect tense is needed because the dejection happened before the arrival of the person mentioned in the sentence.**
 
• **The past perfect tense is formed by using "had" + past participle, so the correct option is "They had been."**
 
• Thus, the correct sentence will be:
 
 
• They had been dejected when he arrived, but now they sparkle with enthusiasm.
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 3 (They was) is incorrect because "was" is the singular past tense form of "be" and does not agree with the plural subject "they."
 
• Option 4 (They were been) is incorrect because "were" is the past tense form of "be" and should not be used with "been."
